argument_summary: The certification defense should be narrowed to a caveated position. The admissible record supports that aggregate readiness currently passes and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which is enough to justify continued launch preparation and a certification packet built around disclosed residual risk. The same record also shows a live weakness in a named launch use case, an incomplete draft mitigation, and a model-card inconsistency. That means the supportable position is not clean certification, but certification conditioned on explicit disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch. On that narrower framing, the packet is defensible and does not require escalation beyond recording the caveat and treating policy closure items as launch-gating follow-through.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is required to support this position. The argument stands on the admissible policy and evidence record alone.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not support certification without material caveats on the current record, because there is neither evidence that no material weakness remains nor an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The policy does permit reliance on monitoring and model-card disclosure as part of risk management, but not as a substitute for the disclosure requirement. The admissible evidence therefore supports a caveated certification posture: the unresolved tax filing assistant limitation must be disclosed for the named launch use case unless an approved risk acceptance is produced before launch.
concessions: Clean compliance is not supportable on the current admissible record.
The draft runbook is incomplete because it lacks at least an accountable owner and alert threshold.
The current model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations conflicts with the unresolved tax filing assistant issue unless corrected or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not eliminate the current disclosure obligation for the known weakness.
